dedupe_keys.name: lpjml lund potsdam jena managed land dynamic global vegetation crop and water model

description: LPJmL is the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research's open-source global model of vegetation, managed land, crops and water. Version 6.0.6 (Zenodo, 25 March 2026) uses a new public input data set by default and fixes all local balance checks. It builds on a methane-enabled version with dynamic wetlands and on the LPJmL4 and LPJmL5 lines. Features added over time include tillage, forest, tea, cotton and oil palm plantations, cover crops, livestock grazing, carbon-costly biological nitrogen fixation and revised nitrogen uptake, each described in a cited paper. Coverage is global. Access is free: the central PIK GitHub repository is archived on Zenodo under AGPL-3.0-or-later. Companion tools include lpjmlkit (an R toolkit, version 1.8.0) and pycoupler (Python coupling, 1.7.0), and LPJmL has been used in code for seasonal crop yield forecasts in Ghana, Kenya and Zimbabwe. Caveats: the programming language and hardware needs are not stated in the Zenodo record, and global runs need large input data. For simulation it supplies gridded crop yields, irrigation water and carbon for climate impact, drought and adaptation scenarios, and feeds the MAgPIE land-use model. Related catalogue records include MAgPIE, the GGCMI outputs and the ISIMIP Repository.
